description: The universe is too vast to explore by hand, but data makes it possible. Our goal with Cosmic Footprint is to turn NASA SPHEREx data into an open, interactive experience for curious enthusiasts hungry for discoveries, scientists searching for answers, and above all children, allowing them to keep dreaming while looking up at the stars. Whatever your background or skills, anyone is welcome, without any exception. Join us on this journey and let's leave our footprint in the cosmos!
summary: A free web tool that finds objects that move in real SPHEREx images, then checks every candidate against independent NASA, ESA and CSA data. Pick a star, press PING, and it aligns twelve SPHEREx images and shows what changed.
details:
Cosmic Footprint Detector is a free browser-based explorer for NASA SPHEREx images that finds objects that move and checks every candidate against independent data.

It fetches small cutouts of real SPHEREx level-2 images, re-aligns each one with its own WCS (North up) and shows them as a blink comparator.

PING stacks many visits, subtracts them and lists moving objects with a false-alarm estimate.

Every candidate is cross-checked with Gaia DR3 proper motion, the SPHEREx spectrum and independent CSA NEOSSat images taken years earlier.

A "time machine" predicts where a star was or will be on any date. SPHEREx pixel flags and an AllWISE overlay help tell real movers from artefacts. A printable report can be generated for each candidate.

For Barnard's Star, the position predicted from Gaia DR3 lands 1.1 arcsec from the real star on a plate-solved NEOSSat image (its 2016 position is 40 arcsec off).

With SPHEREx data, the app measures a proper motion of about 9.6 arcsec/yr, consistent with the 10.4 arcsec/yr catalogued by Gaia.

For researchers, this view is a quick, honest first look at a candidate, with the numbers to back it up. But I also hope to let anyone, a student, a curious citizen, a teacher, look up at the sky and dream. Simple mode, a guided tour and an English/Italian interface make it easy for everyone.

With nothing to install, they can watch real SPHEREx light drift across the screen and see for themselves that the universe is beautiful and unknown.

Tools:

Python (standard library HTTP server, numpy, requests, astropy),

JavaScript with canvas and web workers (no framework),

Cloudflare Workers (optional, used for faster SPHEREx Download),

GitHub and Render for hosting,

Cutouts are read from the public AWS bucket with byte-range requests, with IRSA as fallback.

Code: https://github.com/Giosca05/cosmic-footprint-detector
